transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because something at work has been bothering me for a while. I’m an interpreter and translator, and in the project files I keep seeing the same kind of pattern — small changes in the translation memory, timestamps not quite lining up — and it makes it look like my quality control failed.

I know that might sound a bit hard to explain, and I’m not trying to make trouble. But it seems like certain subcontractors, and one colleague, are… arranging things so the blame lands on me. IT says the audit trail is clean, but I don’t think that really means the record hasn’t been set up that way. I just wanted to talk it through with someone, if that’s okay.
How long have you been noticing this pattern and feeling that colleagues are deliberately arranging things to blame you?

It’s been… I’d say about 11 months now. Not constant every minute or anything, but I started noticing it shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project. That’s when the little irregularities began standing out to me. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people don't seem to notice or hear, related to this situation or otherwise?

No, I don’t think so. I mean… I haven’t heard voices or seen things, if that’s what you mean. It’s more about what’s in the files and the timing of things. I know that probably sounds more reasonable than… other things, right? But no, I’m not noticing sounds or seeing things other people don’t.

Before this situation at work started about 11 months ago, would you say you've generally had a long-standing pattern—going back to your teens or twenties—of finding it hard to trust people or suspecting others' motives, even in unrelated areas of your life like friendships or family?

I don’t think so… not as a long-standing thing. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful with people, maybe a bit private, but I wouldn’t say I went around suspecting friends or family or anything like that.

This feels more specific to what’s been happening at work. At least, that’s how it seems to me. Does that make sense?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a circumscribed, non-bizarre delusional belief (colleagues and subcontractors deliberately manipulating files/timestamps to frame him) persisting for approximately 11 months, exceeding the 1-month duration criterion for delusional disorder. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no other psychotic symptoms (ruling out schizophrenia, which requires ≥2 characteristic symptoms and typically broader functional deterioration). The delusion is well-systematized around a single theme (persecutory/occupational) rather than bizarre or fragmented. Notably, the patient denies a long-standing premorbid pattern of pervasive distrust or suspiciousness predating this episode, which argues against paranoid personality disorder (F60.0) as the primary diagnosis, though it remains a differential to monitor. Overall clinical picture is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type (F22).
